mechanism_log: The system has a clean modular causal structure. Y3 is exclusively determined by X1 and X3 (exact zero gradients for all other inputs; confirmed by flat OAT sweeps). Y4 is primarily driven by X2 and X4 with mild X6 drag. Y1 is driven positively by all six inputs (X4 strongest, then X2, X6, X3, X1, X5 weakest). Y2 is primarily reduced by X3 and X1, but increased by X6 and X2. X5 has a nonlinear saturating effect on Y1 only: large positive effect below X5~0.55, plateaus above. Three inputs (X1, X3, X4) are 'free lunch' — setting them high simultaneously improves Y1, Y2 (helpful direction), and Y3/Y4. The two core trade-off levers are X2 (Y1+Y4 vs Y2) and X6 (Y1 vs Y4+Y2).

The Pareto structure is: set X1=X3=1.0 (free lunch), X5≥0.55 (saturated), then trade off via X2 (scale Y1/Y4 vs Y2), X4 (super-linear Y1/Y4 boost but also raises Y2 at high X2), and X6 (shifts Y1 vs Y4 and complex Y2 effect). A new Pareto trade-off axis emerged: at X2=1.0, reducing X4 from 1.0 to 0.7 lowers Y2 from 0.362 to 0.286 while keeping Y1=0.681 and Y4=0.282 — creating new Pareto-optimal points in the moderate-Y1/lower-Y2 region that weren't accessible by X2-reduction alone.

The regime-dependent interactions for Y1 and Y2 are most pronounced at the extremes (X2=0.1 vs X2=1.0); intermediate X2 values produce intermediate behavior that neither regime model captures well — a reminder that my causal model was built from boundary explorations
iteration_summaries.next_plan: Budget exhausted at 72/72 evaluations. Final recommendation: use [1,0.9,1,1,0.7,0.1] as the best single-point compromise (Y1=0.822, Y2=0.321, Y3=0.997, Y4=0.305). For Y2-priority applications use [1,0.3,1,1,0.7,0.1] (Y2=0.116, Y1=0.189, Y4=0.129). For Y4-priority use [1,1,1,1,0.7,0.1] (Y4=0.322, Y1=0.948). If additional budget were available, the next priority would be testing X4 reductions at X2=0.9 to map the X4-reduction Pareto curve more densely, and probing the X2*X6 interaction on Y4 to confirm whether a sign flip occurs there as well.
